accepted.s: The Naharkatia–Nunmati–Barauni pipeline is notable as:
o: Asia’s first long-distance cross-country crude pipeline
The first pipeline linking Gujarat with Punjab
accepted.x: The Naharkatia–Nunmati–Barauni pipeline is described as Asia’s first long-distance cross-country crude pipeline.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the pipeline’s historical distinction and its geographical route.
accepted.sec: Pipelines - route and FIRSTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Salaya–Koyali–Mathura — Crude oil
2. HVJ — Natural gas
3. Kandla–Bathinda — Crude oil
4. PM Urja Ganga — Natural gas

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Salaya–Koyali–Mathura and Kandla–Bathinda carry crude oil, while HVJ and PM Urja Ganga carry gas.
accepted.tq: Verify each pipeline against its commodity before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Pipelines - route and FIRSTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Salaya–Koyali–Mathura pipeline originates at Salaya on the:
accepted.x: The Salaya–Koyali–Mathura crude-oil pipeline begins at Salaya on the Gulf of Kutch and supplies the Koyali and Mathura refineries.
accepted.tq: Apply the route-and-location method to identify the coastal origin.
accepted.sec: Pipelines - route and FIRSTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pipelines is operated by GAIL and follows the Hazira–Vijaipur–Jagdishpur route?
accepted.x: The HVJ, or HBJ, pipeline is a GAIL gas pipeline connecting Hazira, Vijaipur and Jagdishpur.
accepted.tq: Expand the abbreviation and match the operator with the route.
accepted.sec: Pipelines - route and FIRSTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the HVJ gas pipeline, consider the following statements:

1. It is approximately 1,750 km long.
2. It feeds power plants at Kawas, Anta and Auraiya.
3. It supplies gas to fertiliser plants at Bijaipur, Sawai Madhopur and Jagdishpur.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The HVJ pipeline is about 1,750 km long and supplies power plants including Kawas, Anta and Auraiya and fertiliser plants including Bijaipur, Sawai Madhopur and Jagdishpur.
accepted.tq: Check the numerical detail and then separate the power-plant and fertiliser-plant beneficiaries.
accepted.sec: Pipelines - route and FIRSTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Paradip–Haldia — Crude-oil pipeline on the eastern coast
PM Urja Ganga — Jagdishpur–Haldia and Bokaro–Dhamra gas routes
HVJ — Crude-oil pipeline from Gujarat to Punjab
Kandla–Bathinda — Crude oil pipeline across Rajasthan and Haryana
accepted.x: HVJ is a gas pipeline from Hazira through Vijaipur to Jagdishpur, not a crude-oil pipeline from Gujarat to Punjab. Kandla–Bathinda is the Gujarat–Punjab crude route.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong commodity-route association rather than merely identifying a familiar pipeline name.
accepted.sec: Pipelines - route and FIRSTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: PM Urja Ganga is intended to:
o: Carry crude oil from Assam to Bihar
Transport coal from Odisha to eastern ports
Connect eastern and north-eastern regions to the national gas grid
Connect Gujarat refineries with northern Punjab
accepted.x: PM Urja Ganga brings eastern and north-eastern regions onto the national gas grid through the Jagdishpur–Haldia and Bokaro–Dhamra routes.
accepted.tq: Identify the infrastructure initiative from its stated regional integration function.
accepted.sec: Pipelines - route and FIRSTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The target length of the national gas network under the One Nation One Gas Grid initiative is:
accepted.x: The One Nation One Gas Grid initiative has a target of a national gas network exceeding 32,000 km.
accepted.tq: Use the scale comparison carefully; the correct target is the middle-high value rather than the largest figure.
accepted.sec: Pipelines - route and FIRSTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes PM Gati Shakti?
o: A GIS-based National Master Plan for multimodal connectivity launched in 2021
A port privatisation programme launched in 2020
A rail electrification programme launched in 2022
A national highway tolling scheme launched in 2016
accepted.x: PM Gati Shakti is a GIS-based National Master Plan for multimodal connectivity launched in 2021.
accepted.tq: Combine the scheme’s exact title, technology and launch year to reject neighbouring initiatives.
accepted.sec: PM Gati Shakti and National Logistics Policy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Master Plan under PM Gati Shakti uses more than:
accepted.x: The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan uses more than 1,700 data layers for GIS-based planning.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the precise magnitude from nearby rounded figures.
accepted.sec: PM Gati Shakti and National Logistics Policy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was launched in 2022 to complement PM Gati Shakti?
accepted.x: The National Logistics Policy was launched in 2022 and complements PM Gati Shakti.
accepted.tq: Use the launch-year distinction to separate a policy from an index and an infrastructure programme.
accepted.sec: PM Gati Shakti and National Logistics Policy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The three-tier institutional structure associated with PM Gati Shakti consists of:
o: NITI Aayog, GST Council and Finance Commission
EGoS, NPG and Technical Support Unit
accepted.x: The three tiers are the Empowered Group of Secretaries, Network Planning Group and Technical Support Unit.
accepted.tq: Match the institutional hierarchy rather than confusing it with related indices.
accepted.sec: PM Gati Shakti and National Logistics Policy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The apex Empowered Group of Secretaries under PM Gati Shakti is chaired by the:
o: Minister of Road Transport and Highways
Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog
accepted.x: The apex EGoS under PM Gati Shakti is headed by the Cabinet Secretary.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority would perform the coordinating role at the apex level.
accepted.sec: PM Gati Shakti and National Logistics Policy  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding logistics in India:

1. The PM Gati Shakti platform brought 16 ministries onto one platform.
2. The apex EGoS presently includes 23 infrastructure and user ministries.
3. The LEADS index has been in use since 2018.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: 16 ministries were brought onto the platform, the apex EGoS has 23 infrastructure and user ministries, and LEADS has been used since 2018.
accepted.tq: Check whether the figures refer to the platform or the apex group before selecting the combination.
accepted.sec: PM Gati Shakti and National Logistics Policy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India’s Logistics Performance Index rank improved from 44 in 2018 to which rank in 2023?
accepted.x: India’s LPI rank improved from 44 in 2018 to 38 in 2023.
accepted.tq: Read the direction of change and retain both the base year and the later rank.
accepted.sec: PM Gati Shakti and National Logistics Policy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Infrastructure Pipeline involved an estimated investment of:
accepted.x: The National Infrastructure Pipeline was estimated at ₹111 lakh crore for the period 2020–25.
accepted.tq: Use the number-and-period pair together to avoid confusing the scale of the programme.
accepted.sec: PM Gati Shakti and National Logistics Policy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The logistics cost in India was reported as approximately what percentage of GDP for 2023–24?
accepted.x: The reported logistics cost was 7.97% of GDP in 2023–24; older estimates of 13–14% are not the current figure stated here.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the current estimate and the older commonly quoted range.
accepted.sec: PM Gati Shakti and National Logistics Policy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Inland water transport uses approximately what proportion of the fuel used by road transport per tonne-kilometre?
accepted.x: Inland water transport uses about one-seventh of the fuel used by road transport per tonne-kilometre. Its fuel use is also about one-third that of rail.
accepted.tq: Compare all three modes on the same tonne-kilometre basis before choosing the fraction.
accepted.sec: Modes compared - cheapest and most energy-efficient freight  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which mode of transport is more energy-efficient than road transport for freight movement?
accepted.x: Railways are more energy-efficient than road transport, supporting a shift from road to rail as part of the net-zero strategy.
accepted.tq: Identify the comparative advantage rather than the absolute fastest or most flexible mode.
accepted.sec: Modes compared - cheapest and most energy-efficient freight  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:

1. Roads are particularly suitable for short-distance and last-mile movement.
2. Rail freight costs about half as much as road freight.
3. Rail freight emits approximately 90% less carbon dioxide than road freight.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Roads provide last-mile reach, while rail has lower cost and substantially lower carbon dioxide emissions than road freight.
accepted.tq: Separate the functional advantage of roads from the cost and emission advantages of rail.
accepted.sec: Modes compared - cheapest and most energy-efficient freight  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the longest navigation canal on the east coast?
accepted.x: The Buckingham Canal, approximately 796 km long, is the longest navigation canal on the east coast.
accepted.tq: Pair the named canal with its stated length and coastal location.
accepted.sec: Modes compared - cheapest and most energy-efficient freight  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding freight transport is correct?
o: Road transport is unsuitable for door-to-door movement.
Pipelines are used mainly for passenger movement.
Air transport is the fastest and costliest per tonne-kilometre.
Road transport is the cheapest of all surface modes.
accepted.x: Air transport is the fastest but costliest per tonne-kilometre. Road transport is costliest among surface modes but offers door-to-door reach.
accepted.tq: Compare speed, cost and reach across modes instead of treating one mode as best on every criterion.
accepted.sec: Modes compared - cheapest and most energy-efficient freight  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which State has the lowest road density in India as stated in the available data?
accepted.x: Kerala has the highest road density, whereas Arunachal Pradesh has the lowest road density in the stated comparison.
accepted.tq: Use the extreme-value contrast and avoid selecting the state associated with the opposite extreme.
accepted.sec: Road density and NH length by state  [other exams]

accepted.s: Rail density is particularly high in which of the following regions?
o: Only the coastal districts of Kerala
The north-eastern hills, Himalaya and Rajasthan desert
Punjab, Haryana and the Ganga plains
The Thar Desert and the eastern Himalaya
accepted.x: Rail density is highest in Punjab, Haryana and the Ganga plains; it is lowest in the north-east, Himalayan region and Rajasthan desert.
accepted.tq: Match the high-density railway region with its geographical concentration.
accepted.sec: Road density and NH length by state  [other exams]

accepted.s: India’s first commercial flight, carrying airmail, was operated between:
accepted.x: India’s first commercial airmail flight operated between Allahabad and Naini on 18 February 1911.
accepted.tq: Retain the exact city pair and date associated with the first service.

accepted.s: India’s first commercial airmail flight took place on:
accepted.x: The first commercial airmail flight in India took place on 18 February 1911.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact year and day from close chronological distractors.
accepted.sec: Airways - UDAN, international airports, FIRST air service, greenfield and carbon-neutral airports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: RCS-UDAN was introduced under which policy framework?
accepted.x: RCS-UDAN was introduced under the National Civil Aviation Policy of 2016.
accepted.tq: Match the scheme with its parent policy and launch context.
accepted.sec: Airways - UDAN, international airports, FIRST air service, greenfield and carbon-neutral airports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The acronym UDAN in the regional connectivity scheme stands for:
accepted.x: UDAN stands for “Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik”.
accepted.tq: Test the exact expansion of the official programme acronym.
accepted.sec: Airways - UDAN, international airports, FIRST air service, greenfield and carbon-neutral airports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which funding mechanism is used under the RCS-UDAN scheme?
accepted.x: RCS-UDAN uses Viability Gap Funding to support regional air connectivity.
accepted.tq: Expand the familiar acronym by identifying the exact financial mechanism.
accepted.sec: Airways - UDAN, international airports, FIRST air service, greenfield and carbon-neutral airports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: According to the stated RCS-UDAN figures, the scheme covers:
o: 657 routes and 93 airports, including heliports and water aerodromes
625 routes and 85 airports, excluding heliports and water aerodromes
657 routes and 120 airports, including only conventional airports
500 routes and 93 airports, including only heliports
accepted.x: The stated RCS-UDAN figures are 657 routes and 93 airports, including heliports and water aerodromes. A later update cited 625 routes and 85 airports by 2025.
accepted.tq: Read the figures together with the qualifying phrase about the types of airfields included.
accepted.sec: Airways - UDAN, international airports, FIRST air service, greenfield and carbon-neutral airports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Modified UDAN envisages how many new destinations and how many passengers over ten years?
accepted.x: Modified UDAN envisages 120 new destinations and 4 crore passengers over ten years.
accepted.tq: Treat the destination and passenger figures as a linked pair.
accepted.sec: Airways - UDAN, international airports, FIRST air service, greenfield and carbon-neutral airports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: What additional funding scheme for air connectivity was included in the Union Budget 2026–27?
accepted.x: The Union Budget 2026–27 added a Seaplane Viability Gap Funding scheme.
accepted.tq: Identify the new transport sub-sector attached to the existing funding mechanism.
accepted.sec: Airways - UDAN, international airports, FIRST air service, greenfield and carbon-neutral airports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Greenfield Airports Policy was introduced in:
accepted.x: The Greenfield Airports Policy was introduced in 2008.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the policy’s year from the later years of aviation and logistics initiatives.
accepted.sec: Airways - UDAN, international airports, FIRST air service, greenfield and carbon-neutral airports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the Greenfield Airports Policy, the number of in-principle approvals and operational airports stated were respectively:
accepted.x: The policy had 24 in-principle approvals, of which 13 were operational, including Navi Mumbai.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversal trap between approvals and operational airports.
accepted.sec: Airways - UDAN, international airports, FIRST air service, greenfield and carbon-neutral airports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the world’s first fully solar-powered airport?
accepted.x: Cochin International Airport is recognised as the world’s first fully solar-powered airport.
accepted.tq: Distinguish solar-powered status from the separate categories of greenfield and carbon-neutral airports.
accepted.sec: Airways - UDAN, international airports, FIRST air service, greenfield and carbon-neutral airports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about India’s civil aviation sector is correct?
o: India is the largest domestic aviation market in the world.
India is the third-largest domestic aviation market.
India’s domestic aviation market ranks below all major Asian markets.
India is the third-largest international aviation market only.
accepted.x: India is the third-largest domestic aviation market.
accepted.tq: Use the exact comparative category—domestic market—rather than substituting international aviation.
accepted.sec: Airways - UDAN, international airports, FIRST air service, greenfield and carbon-neutral airports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Open Sky policy mentioned for Indian aviation applies to:
accepted.x: The Open Sky arrangement mentioned applies to six metro airports, not to every airport in the country.
accepted.tq: Reject the universal option by focusing on the specified number of metro airports.
accepted.sec: Airways - UDAN, international airports, FIRST air service, greenfield and carbon-neutral airports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 replaced the Aircraft Act, 1934 with effect from:
accepted.x: The Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 replaced the Aircraft Act, 1934 from January 2025.
accepted.tq: Link the Act’s year with its effective year and avoid treating them as identical.
